mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in WORKPLACES mobility (rising from -8.6% at t-0w) signals resumption of commuting and office occupancy. This restores weekday retail foot traffic patterns within a 4-week lag, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 8.1 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES declines in 3 of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of GROCERY_PHARM toward baseline (now -0.6%) indicates stabilization of essential-goods purchasing behavior. As panic-buying subsides and confidence in supply chains grows, consumers redirect discretionary spending to RETAIL_REC within 1-2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -6.3% to -0.6% over 3 weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rebounds to below -3% in any of the next 2 weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage remains depressed (-23.7% at t-0w) but shows consistent recovery trend (improving 10.6 points from t-3w). Continued TRANSIT recovery over the next 4 weeks enables commuter access to retail districts, directly lifting RETAIL_REC through increased foot traffic.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by >5 points week-on-week for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -34.3% to -23.7% over 3 weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines in 2 or more of the next 4 weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to rise above -15% by week 4.

mechanism_narrative: Depressed PARKS mobility (-16.9% at t-0w) reflects outdoor-activity constraints. If PARKS recovers sharply over the next 2 weeks, it signals policy relaxation and consumer confidence restoration. This confidence spillover increases discretionary retail visits within the same 2-week window.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -16.9% shows room for recovery
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -10% for 2 consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 14.6% to 10.1% over 3 weeks) indicates people spending less time at home, signaling easing of stay-at-home directives. This policy relaxation directly enables retail reopening and consumer mobility, lifting RETAIL_REC over 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 11% for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 4.5 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 12% in any of the next 4 weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains below -18%.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the next 2 weeks creates a multiplier effect: commuting infrastructure restoration enables office workers to access retail districts. The interaction of both signals is necessary to overcome retail friction; either alone is insufficient.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve by >3 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series show consistent recovery trend
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT declines in week 1 or 2, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed -15% by end of week 2.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved 8.6 points over 3 weeks (from -25.9% to -17.3%), establishing a consistent upward trend. Extrapolating this linear recovery rate forward 4 weeks predicts continued improvement independent of external shocks, assuming no policy reversal.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 8.6 points over 3 weeks at ~2.9 points/week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines by >5 points in any single week over the next 4 weeks, or the trend reverses to negative week-on-week change.

mechanism_narrative: Stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM near baseline combined with sustained RESIDENTIAL decline signals consumer confidence recovery and reduced home-confinement behavior. This dual signal triggers a shift from essential to discretionary spending within 1 week, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM within ±1% of baseline AND RESIDENTIAL below 11%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM spikes below -3% in week 1, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 12%, or RETAIL_REC does not improve in week 1.
